messages.content: I need to settle the hotels for Boston and New York now. Keep the Monday arrival, Wednesday morning train, Friday evening flight, two nights in each city, Tuesday campus meeting, and Friday noon finish exactly as planned. Compare the combinations on full cost and the actual transit and luggage burden.

I have two candidates in each city. I’ll compare the four possible pairings using tax-inclusive room totals, Tuesday and Wednesday travel in Boston, access to the New York appointments, and what happens to your suitcase on Friday. What are the latest quoted details for each property?

Boston: Copley Square Hotel is $612 total for the two nights. They will hold my bag Monday before the room is ready and after checkout Wednesday, though I probably won’t need the latter. It is about an 8-minute walk to Back Bay station. The Tuesday campus meeting is in Cambridge, near Harvard Square.

That makes Copley convenient for the 7:15 a.m. Wednesday Acela: leaving around 6:45 should provide a reasonable station margin. For Tuesday, allow roughly 30-40 minutes by subway, including the walk and transfer, or longer in peak traffic by car. What is the other Boston quote?

The Charles Hotel is $728 total. It is a short walk from Tuesday’s meeting, but they only guarantee luggage storage for registered guests on the check-in and checkout dates during staffed bell-desk hours. Getting to Back Bay station Wednesday would be a taxi, estimated at 20-30 minutes that early.

So the Charles costs $116 more. It saves most of Tuesday’s round-trip commute, likely 50-70 minutes in total, but creates an early Wednesday taxi and more schedule variability before the train. Copley costs less and makes the time-sensitive departure much simpler, while putting the longer travel on Tuesday when the meeting schedule is known.

That favors Copley. Before we decide, do both Boston rooms have a coffee maker and a refrigerator or mini-fridge? Those are useful enough that I want both when comparing hotel rooms, even though they aren’t absolute requirements.

The current room descriptions list a coffee maker and mini-fridge at Copley. The Charles listing confirms a coffee maker but does not confirm a refrigerator in the quoted room category. Since Copley has both, there is no need to relax that criterion for the stronger Boston option. The amenity details should still be reconfirmed with the hotel before payment.

Good. Now New York. The Evelyn is $846 total for Wednesday and Thursday nights. It will accept the suitcase when I arrive from Penn Station Wednesday morning, and on Friday it will hold it after the 11:00 a.m. checkout until 6:00 p.m. The appointments are Wednesday afternoon in Midtown, Thursday near Madison Square, and Friday at noon near Union Square.

The Evelyn is well placed for that sequence. It is walkable to the Thursday site, roughly 15-20 minutes by subway or on foot plus local walking for the Wednesday Midtown appointment, and about 15 minutes on foot to the Friday meeting. Friday bag handling also works: check out before the meeting, leave the suitcase, return around 1:15, and still have several hours before leaving for LaGuardia around 3:45-4:15.

The less expensive option is the LIC Plaza Hotel at $624 total. Wednesday bag drop starts at 10:00 a.m. Checkout Friday is 10:00 a.m., and they will hold luggage only until 2:00 p.m. It would mean taking the subway into Manhattan for every appointment.

LIC Plaza saves $222. From there, estimate about 30-40 minutes to Midtown on Wednesday, 30-40 minutes to Madison Square on Thursday, and 35-45 minutes to Union Square on Friday, each way depending on the connection and walking. The early Friday checkout also leaves a longer gap before the noon meeting, and the 2:00 p.m. storage cutoff would require returning to Queens promptly after the appointment or arranging separate storage in Manhattan.
Can you put all four combinations into totals? Use only the hotel amounts for the main comparison, then note likely extra local travel separately.

Hotel-only totals are: Copley plus Evelyn, $1,458; Copley plus LIC Plaza, $1,236; Charles plus Evelyn, $1,574; Charles plus LIC Plaza, $1,352. The spread from lowest to highest is $338. Relative to Copley plus Evelyn, choosing LIC saves $222, while choosing the Charles adds $116.
And the likely transportation difference? I don’t need false precision, just enough to see whether the cheaper pair is genuinely cheaper.

Copley may require a Boston round-trip subway fare Tuesday, while the Charles likely requires a Wednesday taxi to Back Bay station. In New York, LIC adds at least six cross-river subway rides for the three appointment days, plus the airport trip starts from Queens after a required bag retrieval. The subway fares themselves will not erase the $222 hotel savings, but the LIC option costs several hours of added travel and creates the Friday luggage deadline. Separate Manhattan luggage storage or a car trip could narrow the savings modestly.
What does Friday look like under each New York hotel if the appointment ends at noon as scheduled?

From the Evelyn, walk back after the appointment, retrieve the bag around 1:00-1:30, have lunch nearby, and leave for LaGuardia around 3:45-4:15 for the 7:10 p.m. flight. From LIC Plaza, you would need to take the subway back immediately, aiming to collect the bag by 1:15-1:30 before the 2:00 cutoff. You would then be in Queens with the suitcase roughly five hours before departure. A delayed appointment or subway disruption would make the storage cutoff uncomfortable.
Does LIC at least meet the same room amenity criteria?

Its quoted room lists a coffee maker, but the listing does not confirm a refrigerator or mini-fridge. The Evelyn’s quoted room lists both. LIC could be checked directly if its price were otherwise compelling, but on the current information it also falls short of the room setup available at the Evelyn.
Then compare the two sensible finalists: Copley plus Evelyn against Charles plus Evelyn. Include Tuesday inconvenience, Wednesday train risk, and the full difference.

Copley plus Evelyn is $1,458. Charles plus Evelyn is $1,574, so the Charles pairing costs $116 more. The Charles nearly eliminates Tuesday’s Cambridge commute, but requires an early taxi across Boston for the 7:15 a.m. Wednesday train and introduces traffic and pickup uncertainty. Copley requires the Tuesday subway trip to Harvard Square, but Wednesday becomes an 8-minute walk to Back Bay station. Since Tuesday is a full scheduled day and Wednesday has a fixed train departure, Copley places the inconvenience where it is easier to absorb.

Agreed. Select Copley Square Hotel for Monday and Tuesday nights and the Evelyn for Wednesday and Thursday nights. Give me a clean office-booking record, including the total and all details that still need verification.

Office-booking selection: Copley Square Hotel, check in Monday, June 22 and check out Wednesday, June 24, two nights, quoted tax-inclusive total $612; Evelyn Hotel, check in Wednesday, June 24 and check out Friday, June 26, two nights, quoted tax-inclusive total $846. Combined lodging total: $1,458. Copley is about an 8-minute walk from Back Bay station for the Wednesday 7:15 a.m. train and requires a Tuesday commute to the Harvard Square campus meeting. The Evelyn provides practical access to the Manhattan appointments and has quoted Friday luggage storage after the 11:00 a.m. checkout until 6:00 p.m., supporting retrieval after the noon appointment and departure for LaGuardia around 3:45-4:15. Before booking, verify room categories, itemized tax-inclusive totals, cancellation deadlines, deposit and payment terms, any destination or facility charges, Monday bag drop at Copley, Wednesday morning bag acceptance at the Evelyn, Friday storage and retrieval hours, and that each assigned room includes both a coffee maker and a refrigerator or mini-fridge. The selected flights, Wednesday train, meeting schedule, and two-night split remain unchanged.
